title: SkillsFound
description:
What a search found, as `gather search --json` prints it in the
envelope's `data`: what a front end reads back to list the results and
take one, the TUI's results screen and the panel's search alike.

Derived, and [`Found`] written through it, so what its TypeScript and
its schema say is what serde writes, read off the same attributes,
rather than said again beside a serializer written by hand. Under a
name of its own, since the panel's types are written into one folder, a
file to a name, and a scan's [`crate::scan::Found`] has that one.

asked.description: Each finder asked, in the order it was.

failures.description:
Each finder that failed, and each result dropped, beside the rest,
by its code and in its words.

hits.description:
Each skill, once, in [`Finder::ALL`]'s order and each finder's own:
as `--take` numbers them, from 1.

skipped.description:
Each finder to ask that needs a token, and was given none: sent
nothing.

Finder.description:
A skill directory a search can ask, by the word the marker and a
command line name it by.

Hit.description:
One skill a search found: where it is, as `gather git` takes it, and
what the finders say of it.

Read back as it goes out by a front end that takes one: the TUI from the
line's JSON, and the panel's backend from the task the panel sends it
back in, its repository redacted again either way.

finders.description: Each finder that found it, in the order they were asked.

installs.description: How many times it was installed, where a finder counts that.

name.description:
What it is called, printable: the name a finder gave it, or its
folder's, or its repository's for one at the root.

path.description:
The folder in the repository it is in: none for the root, or where
no finder said, which a take gathers the whole repository from.

reference.description: The branch a finder named, none for the repository's default.

repository.description: The repository it is in, as [`url::canonical`] spells it.

stars.description: How many stars its repository has, where a finder counts them.

Said.description:
An error as a serialized type holds one: its code, for a front end to act
on, and its message, for whoever reads it.

Built where the type is serialized, or kept in what a front end reads
(the workspace's snapshot), in place of the error, since an error
holds what JSON has no shape for (an `io::Error`, a parser's own), and
only these two are meant to leave core. Its fields are public for a
front end that reads the snapshot as Rust rather than as JSON, the TUI.

message.description:
Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as every URL
is: an error can quote one, a source's among them, and what built
the error is no promise that it carries no credential.
